name: Bloomed Garlic Powder
desc: Hydrate garlic powder in an equal amount of water so it tastes like fresh garlic.

source.title: Bloomed Garlic Powder
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 1/2 tsp room-temperature water (equal to the garlic powder)

steps: In a small bowl, stir the garlic powder and water into a smooth paste. Do not heat it at this stage.
Optional: melt the butter in a small skillet over medium-low heat, add the garlic paste and cook, stirring, about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir the paste (or the garlic butter) into your dish. This amount seasons a 4-serving batch of mashed potatoes, soup or sauce; scale the powder and water together.
tips: Hydrating the powder wakes up the enzyme alliinase, which turns alliin into allicin and gives a much stronger fresh-garlic flavor.
Never toast dry garlic powder in fat before hydrating it. Heat destroys the enzyme and the garlic flavor mostly disappears.

references.title: Experiment: Bringing Out the Best in Garlic Powder
references.usedFor: 1/2 tsp powder to 1/2 tsp water ratio, sauteing the hydrated paste in butter, why heating dry powder kills the flavor
